pairs.difference: A: sand shadow under the ball goes muted violet, and the ball's whites stay fairly neutral. B: shadow on the sand is a hot saturated orange-red and the white panels pick up pink and peach. Greens and blues are pure, with the warm tint spread everywhere.
pairs.fix: Make the cast shadow a cooler, duller purple-brown. Keep the white panels near-neutral white, and tone the sand down to a muted tan.

pairs.difference: A: a pure glossy blue target face, a fully saturated green wall and very warm wood. Background chroma is above the real range. B: a mostly white target face, a darker vignetted green wall and a softer wood tone, which gives more rest.
pairs.fix: Tone down the blue and the green wall to calmer, grayer values. Let the white and neutral areas carry more of the target.

pairs.difference: A: the wall shadows and the underside of the unit are a flat, strongly tinted green, with shadow chroma well above real. B: the wall shows yellow-to-lavender variation and the shadows are less saturated. Both cards are nearly all green and white.
pairs.fix: Make the shadows a grayer, darker green instead of a vivid tint. Keep the white unit closer to neutral.

pairs.difference: A: pure royal-blue water and a muted gray-lavender sand. The chest is glossy, but the sand rests the eye. B: orange sand and warm wood, with a cyan gradient behind, so the whole card is warmer and louder.
pairs.fix: Make the sand a pale, desaturated beige. Keep the wood browns more muted and the water a deeper, calmer blue.

pairs.difference: A: an intense orange-red wall and floor that are as loud as the hat's gold band, with a warm cast over everything. B: a dark, muted brown room with real neutrals and darker tinted shadows. Background chroma is far lower there.
pairs.fix: Use a duller, darker brown wood for the wall and floor. Keep the saturated color for the hat only, and put the shadows in a deeper brown-violet.

pairs.difference: A: a green backdrop with teal glass and a red booth that has darker red shading. B: a neon orange-red booth that is pushed to pure hue, and a green vignette glow. Both cards are very saturated.
pairs.fix: Make the booth a deeper, slightly duller crimson with brownish shadows. Calm the green background with a grayer tone.

pairs.difference: A: a clean orange floor with striped light blue wall, and gloves in red with black straps. B: a darker blue gradient wall and glowing gloves, with both subject and background chroma above the real range. Little tells these two apart.
pairs.fix: Make the blue wall less glowing and a more even tone. Let the red gloves use a darker, less neon shade in the folds.

pairs.difference: A: yellow fins with gray panels on purple rings. B: fins with a glowing orange gradient on a brighter magenta-purple that is loud and uniform. Background chroma is high on both and there are few hue families on either.
pairs.fix: Make the purple background deeper and calmer. Give the fins a flatter yellow with fewer glowing orange edges.

pairs.difference: A: a cohesive teal, sand and orange scene, with tidy tones and shadows that keep their color. B: many hue families (orange sand, cyan, dark navy water, red ring), with desaturated dark shadows closer to real.
pairs.fix: Make the water shadows less saturated, and let some of the sand and wood colors grey out.

pairs.difference: A: a vivid hot-pink background and a pure orange trunk, with warm saturated sand. B: a lighter, softer magenta, pale sand and pinkish-white rocks. A is louder on both subject and background.
pairs.fix: Use a softer, lighter pink backdrop. Make the trunk a muted brown and the sand a pale cream.

pairs.difference: A: a lavender-gray wall with a cool purple shadow, so the card has resting neutral color. B: a flat, saturated purple wall next to a pure orange locker, a hue-clash pair at full strength with little neutral.
pairs.fix: Make the wall a duller gray-violet with a cooler shadow. Make the locker a slightly browner orange.

pairs.difference: A: a neon lime slide and saturated blue ladder against a coral-pink wavy background, with subject chroma above the real range. B: a deeper, more natural green with calmer tones.
pairs.fix: Use a deeper, less neon green for the slide. Tone the pink background down and add some gray.

pairs.difference: A: a flat periwinkle background and an orange-yellow player with white earbuds. B: a glowing magenta-purple with a radial bloom around the player. Both have high background chroma.
pairs.fix: Use a flatter, calmer violet without the bright center glow. Make the orange a bit less luminous.

pairs.difference: A: a darker green edge vignette that holds the card down, though the photos are vivid. B: a bright lime-green glow that is uniform and loud, with a cream envelope on top.
pairs.fix: Make the green background darker and less lime. Add a muted edge instead of a glow.

pairs.difference: A: a peach striped wall and fruit with normal chroma, where the wall rests the eye. B: a wood table whose chroma is lower than A's, with fruit pushed above the real chroma range and glassy highlights.
pairs.fix: Dull the fruit colors slightly, especially the orange and watermelon red. Make the table a duller tan.

pairs.difference: A: a deep saturated blue door, olive-green ivy and orange frame. B: a cream wall, a lighter blue door, an orange bow and pastel flowers. Both are in the real ranges and my vector gives no clear reason to choose.

pattern: Generated cards push everything to full strength. The backgrounds are as loud as the hero, and there is little neutral or gray to rest the eye. Highlights glow with a bloom, whites tint pink or peach, and cast shadows turn hot orange or red instead of the cool, muted purple-brown on the real cards. The real cards keep grays and neutrals and let the background sit back.
